notes.cover-title: NOVA sequences warehouse tasks and connects equipment. Use shipping deadlines and equipment status to illustrate how it adjusts the work sequence.
notes.challenge-title: Empathy: Highlight three recurring pain points—disconnected priorities, growing multi-vendor integration cost, and tribal knowledge in exception handling.
notes.positioning-title: Product suite: Clearly separate execution (WES/WCS), web operations (Workspace), and 3D spatial monitoring (Studio). Note that Studio can also connect to existing systems.
notes.architecture-title: Concrete hook: Walk through a delayed outbound wave—spotting the lagging wave in Workspace and pinpointing the equipment fault in Studio.
notes.workflow-title: End-to-end load flow: Receiving, storage, transfer, and sorting/dispatch run as one connected workflow with results and exceptions reported upstream.
notes.foundation-title: Architecture value: Reuse Core Engine and Common Services while isolating site-specific rules and protocols in Edge Extensions to reduce rework.
notes.wes-title: WES detail: Separate business decisions (Operation) from floor sequencing and bottleneck adjustments (Orchestration).
notes.wcs-title: WCS credibility: Emphasize separating command acceptance from actual completion and verifying execution state before retries to prevent duplicate moves.
notes.interfaces-title: System integration: System Agents normalize APIs, async events and legacy/batch channels with clear acceptance, retry and reconnection contracts.
notes.agents-title: Equipment integration: Cover storage, transport, sorting and picking while setting clear boundaries with PLC controllers and AMR fleet managers.
notes.workspace-title: Workspace overview: One web interface for live status, master data, task tracking, equipment alarms, role-based access and scheduled jobs.
notes.workspace-operations-title: Workspace operations: Compare wave progress alongside active equipment alarms to find root causes faster.
notes.workspace-management-title: Workspace admin: Show governance controls—role-based permissions and auditable scheduled job runs.
notes.studio-title: Studio overview: Combine full-line overview and close-up multi-level rack inspection in one 3D view. Connects to NOVA or existing WMS/WCS.
notes.offering-title: Commercial flexibility (key slide): Customers can adopt only the 3D scene viewer, add monitoring panels, or deploy full NOVA WES/WCS integration.
notes.studio-examples-title: Studio 3D line view: Combine branching conveyor paths with throughput and availability panels.
notes.studio-examples-more-title: Studio 3D view: Inspect multi-tier racks and highlight faulty sections visually for faster dispatch to the floor.
notes.studio-video-title: The first video shows how the conveyor lines connect from several viewpoints. The second shows where an alarm occurs and how Studio displays equipment status.
notes.adoption-title: Adoption options: Keep existing WMS and start at a bottleneck. Supports integrated or separated WES/WCS across on-premise, air-gapped or hybrid sites.
notes.delivery-title: Phased delivery: Reduce risk across four phases—assess, core rollout, expand, optimize—validated with failure, reconnection and regression tests.
notes.measurement-title: Honest KPIs: Agree on baseline scope and formulas first—traceability, response time, manual intervention and latency—before comparing before/after results.
notes.references-title: These cases cover retail, pharmaceutical and general logistics sites. Use site A’s daily volume, site B’s SKU count and site C’s hourly volume to describe each site’s scale.
notes.contact-title: Closing: Propose an initial scoping workshop built around the three-item discovery checklist on the right.
